One blanket AI training block could take your brand out of Gemini answers.

In this clip Hannah and I cover what one blanket block on AI training can cost a brand. Google treats a shared-token opt-out as blocking Google-Extended, which could take you out of Gemini answers too.

Keep any opt-out to the paths you are protecting. Give AI your current and proposed robots.txt and it flags anything that would block Googlebot or Bingbot by accident.

Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/shared-ai-training-opt-out-robots-txt/
clips.text: A brand hears "opt out of AI training", feels protective, and adds one blanket block. What does that cost them? With Google, possibly more than they meant. Google's post says sites that specifically allow Google-Extended are eligible to appear in Gemini app answers and get clicks from them. And a shared-token opt-out counts as blocking Google-Extended. So one tidy line across the whole site could take you out of Gemini answers too.

clips.linkedin:
Before anyone touches robots.txt, find out which content you actually sell or license.

In this clip Hannah and I cover the first job to hand over. Before anyone edits robots.txt, someone needs to know which parts of the site carry paid, gated or licensed content.

Give AI your sitemap or a crawl export and a short note on what you sell or license. It hands back a list of directories with a draft path-level rule for each one, and a person still checks it against the contracts.

The podcast voices are AI-generated, and mine is a clone of my own voice.

Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/shared-ai-training-opt-out-robots-txt/
clips.text: Right, so what do you hand over? Get AI on this. First, the inventory of which parts of the site carry paid, gated or licensed content. Give it your sitemap or a crawl export and a short note on what you sell or license, and it hands back a list of directories with a draft path-level rule for each one. A person still checks it against the contracts.
